norms.heading: Proof of service.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 506 Commencement of Actions and General Provisions

norms.text:
1. Every officer to whom any writ of process shall be directed and delivered for service shall make return thereof in writing of the time, place and manner of service of such writ, and shall sign his name to such return.

2. If service of such process is, by order of the court, directed to and delivered to a person, other than an officer, for service, such person shall make affidavit as to the time, place and manner of his service thereof.

3. Service by mail shall be proved by a certificate of the clerk that he has mailed a copy of the summons and of the petition as required by law and the order of the court and by the return registered mail receipt mentioned in subsection 2 of section 506.160, which shall be filed as a paper in the particular lawsuit.

4. Service by publication shall be proved by an affidavit showing the dates upon which and the newspaper in which the notice of publication was published. A copy of the notice shall be attached to the affidavit which shall be filed in the cause. The clerk's certificate that he has mailed a copy of the notice to each defendant whose address was stated in the motion for order of publication and the date of the mailing shall likewise be filed.

5. No person shall be arrested, held to bail, or imprisoned, on any mesne process or execution founded upon any civil action whatsoever.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose à l’autorité compétente d’informer l’huissier des diligences accomplies et de lui transmettre les justificatifs, tenus à la disposition de la juridiction. Rule 54.20 et RSMo 506.180 organisent la preuve, les retours et le dépôt au dossier, mais sans mécanisme identique d’information par une autorité de remise.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the competent authority to report its efforts to the process server and transmit delivery records, which must be available to the court. Rule 54.20 and RSMo 506.180 govern proof, returns, and filing, but do not provide the same authority-to-server reporting mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article précise les éléments qui déterminent les dates d’expédition, de remise et de réception, notamment le cachet postal et l’avis de réception. Rule 54.20(d) et RSMo 506.180(3) organisent la preuve du service postal par certificat et récépissé; Rule 54.20(a)(3) reconnaît aussi l’accusé de réception comme preuve.
correspondences.note_en: The article specifies how dispatch, delivery, and receipt dates are established, including the postal stamp and acknowledgment of receipt. Rule 54.20(d) and RSMo 506.180(3) provide proof of mailed service through a clerk’s certificate and returned receipt; Rule 54.20(a)(3) also treats acknowledgment as proof.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 687 règle l’information de l’autorité requérante et la transmission des procès-verbaux ou récépissés constatant la remise. La Rule 54.20 et RSMo 506.180 organisent la preuve et le retour de la signification par rapports, affidavits ou récépissés, sans prévoir le rôle spécifique du procureur ni de l’autorité requérante.
correspondences.note_en: Article 687 governs notice to the requesting authority and transmission of records or receipts proving delivery. Rule 54.20 and RSMo 506.180 govern proof and return of service through returns, affidavits, or receipts, but do not provide for the prosecutor’s or requesting authority’s specific role.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose, en cas de signification à personne, une information verbale du débiteur et la mention de cette formalité dans l’acte. Les règles du Missouri organisent la signification personnelle et sa preuve par retour ou affidavit, mais n’exigent pas cette information verbale spécifique.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires oral communication to the debtor upon personal service and a statement of that formality in the service act. Missouri rules govern personal service and proof by return or affidavit, but do not require this specific oral notice.

correspondences.note_fr: L’huissier doit transmettre à la juridiction ayant rendu l’injonction une copie de l’acte de signification. Les textes du Missouri organisent la preuve et le dépôt du retour de signification, mais n’imposent pas cette transmission spécifique à la juridiction ayant rendu l’injonction.
correspondences.note_en: The bailiff must send the issuing court a copy of the service document. The Missouri provisions govern proof and filing of service returns, but do not impose this specific transmission to the court that issued the order.

norms.heading: Court may allow process, return or proof of service to be amended, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 506 Commencement of Actions and General Provisions

norms.text: At any time in its discretion and upon such terms as it deems just, the court may allow any process, return, or proof of service thereof to be amended, unless it clearly appears that material prejudice would result to the substantial rights of the party against whom the process issued.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet de couvrir la nullité par une régularisation ultérieure, sous réserve de l’absence de forclusion et de grief. Le RSMo 506.190 autorise la modification d’un acte de procédure en l’absence de préjudice substantiel, mais ne prévoit pas cette règle générale de nullité ni la forclusion.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows nullity to be cured by later regularization, subject to no forfeiture and no prejudice. RSMo 506.190 permits amendment of process, return, or proof of service absent material prejudice, but does not establish a general nullity or forfeiture rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 121 écarte le prononcé d’une nullité susceptible d’être couverte lorsque sa cause a disparu au moment où le juge statue. RSMo 506.190, Rule 55.33, RSMo 511.270 et Rule 57.07 organisent diverses corrections ou cures d’irrégularités, mais dans des domaines et selon des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 121 prevents a curable nullity from being pronounced when its cause has disappeared by the time of decision. RSMo 506.190, Rule 55.33, RSMo 511.270, and Rule 57.07 provide various mechanisms for correcting or curing irregularities, but in narrower contexts and under different conditions.

norms.heading: Service on nonresidents, generally.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 506 Commencement of Actions and General Provisions

norms.text: Service of process outside the state and return thereof shall be made in accordance with supreme court rule 54.20.(b).
revisor_notes: *Interested persons should note the following was part of H.B. 1660 passed by the 84th G.A., 1988.

correspondences.note_fr: Les dispositions du Missouri concernent le service ou la notification à l’extérieur de l’État, notamment les modalités de signification et le retour ou la preuve du service. L’article 683 établit un cadre plus large pour les notifications judiciaires et extrajudiciaires internationales, sous réserve des règlements européens et des traités.
correspondences.note_en: The Missouri provisions concern service or notification outside the state, including methods of service and the return or proof of service. Article 683 establishes a broader framework for international judicial and extrajudicial notifications, subject to European regulations and treaties.

norms.heading: Use of highways by nonresidents shall constitute an agreement.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 506 Commencement of Actions and General Provisions

norms.text:
The use and operation of a motor vehicle or trailer in this state on the public highways thereof by a person who is a nonresident of this state shall be deemed:

(1) An agreement by him that he, his executor, administrator or other legal representative shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the courts of this state in all civil actions and proceedings brought against him, his executor, administrator or other legal representative by either a resident or a nonresident plaintiff, for damages to person or property, including actions for death, growing or arising out of such use and operation; and

(2) An appointment by such nonresident, his executor, administrator or other legal representative of the secretary of state of Missouri as his lawful attorney and agent upon whom may be served all process in suits pertaining to such actions and proceedings;

(3) An agreement by such nonresident that any process in any suit so served shall be of the same legal force and validity as if personally served in this state.

norms.heading: Service of process.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 506 Commencement of Actions and General Provisions

norms.text:
1. Service of process under sections 506.200 to 506.320 shall be made by delivering a copy of the summons, with a copy of the petition attached, to the secretary of state of Missouri at his office, or in his absence, to the chief clerk of the secretary of state, at his office, and such service shall be sufficient service upon such nonresident.

2. The secretary of state shall immediately mail to the defendant, and to each of them if there be more than one, by restricted, registered mail, addressed to the defendant at his last known address, residence or place of abode a notice of such service and a copy of such process and petition.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose un avis postal supplémentaire le jour même ou le premier jour ouvrable, avec copie de l’acte, après certaines significations. Les textes Missouri prévoient des notifications postérieures par courrier dans des contextes particuliers, notamment après signification à un fonctionnaire ou en matière de saisie-arrêt, mais pas une règle générale identique.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires an additional postal notice, generally the same day or next business day, with a copy of the document, after specified forms of service. Missouri provides comparable post-service notices in specific settings—service through officials and garnishment—but no identical general rule.

norms.heading: Notification other than by mail.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 506 Commencement of Actions and General Provisions

norms.text: In lieu of mailing such notification to the defendant in a foreign state, plaintiff may cause said notification to be personally served in the foreign state on the defendant by an adult person not a party to the suit by delivering said notification to the defendant or by offering to make such delivery in case defendant refuses to accept same, or by having said notification served on defendant by an officer duly qualified to serve legal process in the state or jurisdiction where the defendant is found and the officer's return showing such service to have been made filed in the case on or before the return day of the process, or within such further time as the court may allow. Upon such service a general judgment may be taken against defendant or defendants.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 479 exige que le jugement rendu contre une partie résidant à l’étranger constate expressément les diligences accomplies pour l’informer de l’acte introductif. Les dispositions du Missouri organisent la signification et sa preuve à l’étranger ainsi que le jugement par défaut, mais n’exigent pas cette constatation expresse dans le jugement.
correspondences.note_en: Article 479 requires a judgment against a party residing abroad to expressly record the efforts made to inform the defendant of the initiating process. The Missouri provisions regulate service and proof of service abroad and default judgments, but do not require that express recital in the judgment.

correspondences.note_fr: Les dispositions du Missouri concernent le service ou la notification à l’extérieur de l’État, notamment les modalités de signification et le retour ou la preuve du service. L’article 683 établit un cadre plus large pour les notifications judiciaires et extrajudiciaires internationales, sous réserve des règlements européens et des traités.
correspondences.note_en: The Missouri provisions concern service or notification outside the state, including methods of service and the return or proof of service. Article 683 establishes a broader framework for international judicial and extrajudicial notifications, subject to European regulations and treaties.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit la notification d’actes étrangers par remise simple ou signification. Les règles du Missouri organisent la signification personnelle hors de l’État, mais selon des conditions tenant notamment à l’auteur de la signification et à la procédure locale.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows foreign-originating acts to be served by simple delivery or formal service. Missouri provisions govern personal service outside the state, but under conditions concerning who may serve and compliance with the local procedure.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS

norms.text: Proof of the mailing or personal delivery of said notification to such nonresident by an adult person not an officer serving same shall be made by affidavit of the party doing said acts. All affidavits of service shall be endorsed upon or attached to the original papers to which they relate and including the returned registry receipt shall be forthwith filed with the court in which such action is filed and pending.

correspondences.note_fr: Lorsque le ministère public intervient, la remise est simple, gratuite et constatée par récépissé indiquant la date et les conditions. Le Missouri prévoit la remise personnelle et la preuve par retour, affidavit ou constat du mode et du moment de la signification, sans reprendre ce rôle du ministère public.
correspondences.note_en: When the public prosecutor performs the notification, delivery is simple, free, and evidenced by a receipt stating its date and conditions. Missouri provides personal delivery and proof through a return, affidavit, or record of the time and manner of service, but has no equivalent prosecutorial role.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS

norms.heading: Dismissal of action, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 506 Commencement of Actions and General Provisions

norms.text:
Notwithstanding any court costs which have been paid, the court shall dismiss an offender's civil action or appeal from a judgment in a civil action at any time, including before service on the defendant, if the court determines any of the following:

(1) The allegation of indigency is untrue;

(2) The litigation is frivolous, malicious or fails to state a claim upon which relief may be granted; or

(3) The defendant is immune from the cause of action.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 499-1 permet d’accorder une provision pour le procès et de rejeter rapidement une demande manifestement infondée. La Rule 74.04 organise le summary judgment et les textes relatifs au rejet permettent certaines sorties anticipées, mais aucun ne prévoit ces pouvoirs spécifiques pour la participation au débat public.
correspondences.note_en: Article 499-1 permits a litigation advance and rapid dismissal of a manifestly unfounded claim. Rule 74.04 provides summary judgment, while the dismissal provisions allow some early dispositions, but none establishes these specific powers for public-debate participation.

norms.heading: Court to review complaint.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 506 Commencement of Actions and General Provisions

norms.text:
1. The court shall review, before docketing, if feasible, or as soon as practicable after docketing, a complaint in a civil action in which an offender seeks redress from a governmental entity, officer or employee and shall identify cognizable claims or dismiss the complaint or any portion of the complaint, if the complaint:

(1) Is frivolous, malicious or fails to state a claim upon which relief may be granted; or

(2) Seeks monetary relief from a defendant who is immune from such relief.

2. If a civil action or appeal of a civil judgment is dismissed on the grounds that it was frivolous, malicious or failed to state a claim upon which relief may be granted, the court may order attorneys' fees and court costs to the defendant, and payment shall be made pursuant to section 506.372.

norms.heading: Exhaustion of administrative remedies required — dismissal — limitations on remedies.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 506 Commencement of Actions and General Provisions

norms.text:
1. No civil action may be brought by an offender, except for a constitutional deprivation, until all administrative remedies are exhausted.

2. If a claim is, on its face, frivolous, malicious, fails to state a claim upon which relief may be granted or seeks monetary relief from a defendant who is immune from such relief, the court may dismiss the underlying claim without first requiring the exhaustion of administrative remedies.

3. A civil action pursued by an offender in a court of this state alleging in whole or in part a violation of federal law shall be subject to all limitations on remedies established by federal law.

norms.heading: Actions in which outstate service is authorized — jurisdiction of Missouri courts applicable, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 506 Commencement of Actions and General Provisions

revisor_notes: (1969) This section is procedural and remedial and applies retrospectively to causes of action which accrued before its passage. State ex rel. Nichols v. Fuller (A.), 449 S.W.2d 11.

(1970) The Missouri "Long-Arm Statute" is constitutional. State ex rel. Deere & Co. v. Pinnell (Mo.), 454 S.W.2d 889; State ex rel. Birdsboro Corp. v. Kimberlin (Mo.), 461 S.W.2d 292; Fulton v. Southern Pacific Co. (W.D.Mo.), 320 F.Supp. 45.
(1970) This section does not deny due process. State ex rel. Deere and Co. v. Pinnell (Mo.), 454 S.W.2d 889.

(1973) The phrase "commission of a tortious act within this state" includes extraterritorial acts producing actionable consequence in Missouri, also it is not necessary that cause of action pleaded sound in tort in order to confer jurisdiction under this section. Fulton v. Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific Railroad Co. (C.A. Mo.), 481 F.2d 326.

(1973) A foreign corporation which manufactures a product for use in Missouri is subject to extraterritorial jurisdiction on the ground that a tortious act is committed within this state when the dealer seeks indemnification from the manufacturer by way of impleader, and mandamus is the appropriate remedy to compel the impleader of such manufacturer. State ex rel. Apco Oil Corp. v. Turpin (A.), 490 S.W.2d 400.
(1976) Held that evidence sustained finding of sufficient contact to give forum state jurisdiction. State ex rel. Peoples Bank, etc. v. Stussie (A.), 536 S.W.2d 934.

(1976) Retention of unpaid draft for an unreasonable time by a Nebraska Bank which resulted in damages to Missouri bank was not sufficient to justify in personam jurisdiction by Missouri court. State ex rel. Bank of Gering v. Schoenlaub (Mo.), 540 S.W.2d 31.
(1976) Service of process by sheriff of another state does not come under verity rule and may be collaterally attacked. Germanese v. Champlin (A.), 540 S.W.2d 109.

(1984) In a declaratory judgment action relating to defendant's patent, the existence of a business relationship between the nonresident defendant corporation and a Missouri distributor of the product in question was held sufficient to confer personal jurisdiction over the defendant corporation under subdivision (1) of subsection 1. Aluminum Housewares Co., Inc. v. Chip Clip Corp. (E.D. Mo.) 609 F.Supp. 358.

(1984) Telephone conversations and written correspondence were insufficient contacts under the due process clause to justify the exercise of personal jurisdiction over a nonresident defendant on a contract claim, and were therefore also insufficient to satisfy the Missouri "long arm" statute. Inst. Food Marketing v. Golden State Strawberries (8th Cir.), 747 F.2d 448.

(1985) Assertion of personal jurisdiction over a nonresident defendant did not violate the due process clause where the defendant "transacted business within the state" by selling and shipping conveyor belts to a Missouri buyer for installation in Illinois. Precision Const. Co. v. J.A. Slattery Co., Inc. (8th Cir.), 765 F.2d 114.

(1986) Where Colorado savings and loan association solicited participation of Missouri savings and loan association in construction loans, negotiated agreement in Missouri, and where contract became binding through acceptance in Missouri, the exercise of personal jurisdiction over Colorado savings and loan did not violate due process. St. Louis Fed. Sav. and Loan v. Silverado Banking. 626 F.Supp. 379 (E.D. Mo.).

(1986) A foreign corporation which does no more than manufacture a product which eventually is used in this state does not have sufficient contact with the state for a circuit court to exercise jurisdiction over such corporation. State v. Adolf, 718 S.W.2d 550 (Mo.App.).

(1987) Communication through the mails and by telephone to seller before contract was made and visit to seller in this state to perfect product design after contract was made by buyer are contacts sufficient to constitute the transaction of business in this state, thus subjecting nonresident buyer to jurisdiction of court of this state pursuant to this section without violating due process principles. Watlow Elec. Mfg. v. Sam Dick Industries, 734 S.W.2d 295 (Mo.App.).

(1991) Where parties executed stock purchase agreement, promissory note to effectuate the agreement, and guaranty agreement on the indebtedness in Missouri and negotiations leading up to contract were conducted in Missouri, there was sufficient minimum contacts to satisfy federal due process and was sufficient to confer jurisdiction under Missouri Long-Arm Act, regardless of whether defendant also engaged in the transaction of business within the state. Portnoy v. Defiance, Inc., 951 F.2d 169 (8th Cir.).

(2000) Nonresident trademark infringement defendant's website, which had not been accessed by any Missouri resident, did not give rise to sufficient contacts with state to allow court to exercise personal jurisdiction. Uncle Sam's Outfitters, Inc. v. Uncle Sam's Army Navy Outfitters-Manhattan, Inc., 96 F.Supp.2d 919 (E.D.Mo.).

(2000) Foreign microbrewery, which advertised and sold beer club memberships to state residents using the internet and telephones and delivered beer to residents, was subject to personal jurisdiction; state interest in regulation of the sale and delivery of alcoholic beverages outweighed burden on defendant. State ex rel. Nixon v. Beer Nuts, Ltd., 29 S.W.3d 828 (Mo.App.E.D.).

(2002) Maintenance of an internet website allowing visitors to site to make hotel room reservations is not sufficient contact with Missouri to subject defendant to personal jurisdiction for alleged tort that occurred in another state. Bell v. Imperial Palace Hotel/Casino, 200 F.Supp.2d 1082 (E.D.Mo.).

norms.heading: Service, how made — affidavit.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 506 Commencement of Actions and General Provisions

norms.text:
1. Service of process upon any person who is subject to the jurisdiction of the courts of this state, as provided in section 506.500, may be made by personally serving the process upon the defendant outside this state, or upon a corporation by serving the process upon a managing officer or any person or corporation who shall be designated as a registered agent by such corporation in any of the several states, and shall have the same force and effect as though the process had been served within this state.

2. The process, together with a copy of the petition, and necessary fees shall be sent to a court of record or court officer at the place where the defendant may be served with process, and may be personally served upon the defendant by the person authorized to serve process at that place.

3. An affidavit of the person serving the process shall be returned to the office of the clerk or judge from which it issued. The affidavit shall state the time, manner and place of service of the process and of the copy of the petition. The court may consider the affidavit, or any other competent evidence, in determining whether service has been properly made.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe, pour les notifications effectuées hors de certains territoires ou à l’étranger, la date d’expédition comme date de notification à l’égard de l’expéditeur, avec une règle subsidiaire de réception par le parquet. La Rule 90.03(b) prévoit que certains envois sont accomplis dès leur expédition, tandis que les autres textes organisent surtout la preuve de la signification hors de l’État, sans fixer une règle générale de computation.
correspondences.note_en: The article treats the dispatch date as the notification date, for the sender, when service is made in specified overseas territories or abroad, with a fallback based on receipt by the competent public prosecutor. Rule 90.03(b) makes certain mailed service complete upon mailing, while the other provisions mainly govern proof of out-of-state service and do not establish a general computation rule.

correspondences.note_fr: Les dispositions du Missouri concernent le service ou la notification à l’extérieur de l’État, notamment les modalités de signification et le retour ou la preuve du service. L’article 683 établit un cadre plus large pour les notifications judiciaires et extrajudiciaires internationales, sous réserve des règlements européens et des traités.
correspondences.note_en: The Missouri provisions concern service or notification outside the state, including methods of service and the return or proof of service. Article 683 establishes a broader framework for international judicial and extrajudicial notifications, subject to European regulations and treaties.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 684 organise la notification internationale par remise au parquet et transmission ministérielle ou conventionnelle, avec des règles particulières pour les États et bénéficiaires d’immunité. Les textes du Missouri prévoient la signification personnelle hors de l’État et son acheminement à une autorité locale, sans mécanisme équivalent de parquet ou de voie diplomatique.
correspondences.note_en: Article 684 routes international service through the public prosecutor and, ordinarily, the Minister of Justice or diplomatic channels, with special treatment for states and immunized persons. Missouri provides personal service outside the state and transmission to a local court officer, but no equivalent prosecutor or diplomatic-channel mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 685 règle l’acheminement de deux copies par le procureur au ministre de la justice ou à l’autorité désignée, ainsi que l’éventuelle ordonnance du juge. Le Missouri prévoit l’envoi du processus et de la requête à une juridiction ou à un officier étranger habilité, mais sans transmission ministérielle ni ordonnance équivalente.
correspondences.note_en: Article 685 governs sending two copies through the prosecutor to the Minister of Justice or a designated authority, including a possible judicial transmission order. Missouri permits sending process and the petition to a foreign court or authorized officer, but has no equivalent ministerial transmission or judicial-order procedure.

norms.heading: Personal judgment authorized — default judgment, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 506 Commencement of Actions and General Provisions

norms.text:
1. When jurisdiction over a person, firm, or corporation who is outside this state is acquired in accordance with the provisions of sections 506.500 and 506.510, the court shall have the power to render a personal judgment against such person, firm, or corporation.

2. No default judgment shall be entered until the expiration of at least thirty days after service of process. A default judgment rendered on service of process provided by sections 506.500 to 506.520 may be set aside only on a showing which would be timely and sufficient to set aside a default judgment rendered on ordinary service of process within this state.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 479 exige que le jugement rendu contre une partie résidant à l’étranger constate expressément les diligences accomplies pour l’informer de l’acte introductif. Les dispositions du Missouri organisent la signification et sa preuve à l’étranger ainsi que le jugement par défaut, mais n’exigent pas cette constatation expresse dans le jugement.
correspondences.note_en: Article 479 requires a judgment against a party residing abroad to expressly record the efforts made to inform the defendant of the initiating process. The Missouri provisions regulate service and proof of service abroad and default judgments, but do not require that express recital in the judgment.

norms.heading: Citation of law — definitions — application of foreign prohibited, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 506 Commencement of Actions and General Provisions

norms.text:
1. This section shall be known and may be cited as the "No Foreign Laws Act".

2. As used in this section, the following terms mean:

(1) "Foreign law", any law, legal framework, legal code, or system, including religious law when invoked as a substitute for a state or federal law, derived from a jurisdiction outside of any state or territory of the United States, including international organizations and tribunals;

(2) "Fundamental rights", rights guaranteed by the Constitution of Missouri and the Constitution of the United States, including, but not limited to, due process, equal protection, freedom of religion, freedom of speech, and rights related to marriage, child custody, and property.

3. The application of any foreign law that denies the parties fundamental rights shall be prohibited and render the following void and unenforceable:

(1) A ruling or decision of any state court, arbitration panel, or administrative agency;

(2) A contract or contractual provision, if severable, that provides for the choice of any foreign law; and

(3) A contract or contractual provision, if severable, that grants jurisdiction to a foreign tribunal.

4. No court shall enforce or apply:

(1) A judgment, decree, or arbitration decision if it relies, in whole or in part, on any foreign law that violates the fundamental rights of a party;

(2) A contract or contractual provision, if severable, that provides for the choice of any foreign law where the enforcement or application would be in violation of a party's fundamental rights; or

(3) Foreign law in matters involving marriage, divorce, child custody, adoption, or inheritance if such enforcement or application would be inconsistent with fundamental rights or public policy.

5. The provisions of this section shall not be construed to:

(1) Disapprove or abrogate existing precedent of the Missouri supreme court;

(2) Limit adjudication of ecclesiastical matters of a religious organization, including the selection, appointment, discipline, or removal of clergy or interpretation of doctrine;

(3) Apply to corporations, partnerships, or associations that voluntarily subject themselves to any foreign law or foreign courts; or

(4) Apply where federal law preempts state law, including obligations under treaties or international agreements.

correspondences.note_fr: Le tribunal arbitral statue selon les règles de droit, sauf mission d’amiable composition. Le RSMo 506.602 encadre seulement l’application d’une loi étrangère portant atteinte aux droits fondamentaux dans une décision arbitrale, sans régler de manière générale le choix entre droit et amiable composition.
correspondences.note_en: The arbitral tribunal must decide according to law unless empowered to act as an amiable compositeur. RSMo 506.602 only restricts the application of foreign law that violates fundamental rights in an arbitration decision; it does not generally regulate merits law or amiable composition.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article interdit l’exequatur d’une sentence manifestement contraire à l’ordre public et impose la motivation du refus. RSMo 506.602 interdit l’exécution de certaines décisions arbitrales fondées sur une loi étrangère attentatoire aux droits fondamentaux; les autres textes prévoient des refus pour contrariété à l’ordre public dans des procédures de reconnaissance distinctes, sans exigence équivalente de motivation.
correspondences.note_en: The article bars exequatur of an award manifestly contrary to public policy and requires reasons for refusal. RSMo 506.602 bars enforcement of certain arbitration decisions based on foreign law violating fundamental rights; the other provisions provide public-policy refusal grounds in distinct recognition proceedings, without an equivalent reasoning requirement.

norms.heading: Prosecution in name of real party in interest.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text: Every action shall be prosecuted in the name of the real party in interest, but an executor, administrator, personal representative, guardian, conservator, trustee of an express trust, a party with whom or in whose name a contract has been made for the benefit of another, or a party authorized by statute may sue in his own name in such representative capacity without joining with him the party for whose benefit the action is brought; and when a statute so provides, an action for the use or benefit of another shall be brought in the name of the state of Missouri.

correspondences.note_en: Article 31 permits actions by persons with a legitimate interest, subject to statutory qualifications. Rule 52.01 and RSMo 507.010 require prosecution by the real party in interest, but do not state the broader French rule or its exceptions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 32 rend irrecevable la prétention formée par ou contre une personne dépourvue du droit d’agir. Rule 55.27 permet de soulever l’absence de capacité juridique, et Rule 52.01 ainsi que RSMo 507.010 exigent que l’action soit engagée par la real party in interest, mais ces textes ne recouvrent pas exactement toute la notion française de droit d’agir.
correspondences.note_en: Article 32 makes a claim inadmissible when brought by or against a person lacking the right to sue or be sued. Rule 55.27 permits an objection based on lack of legal capacity, while Rule 52.01 and RSMo 507.010 require the real party in interest; these provisions do not fully match the broader French concept.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 414 limite la représentation d’une partie à une seule personne habilitée par la loi. Les textes du Missouri autorisent certaines personnes à agir en qualité représentative sans joindre le bénéficiaire, mais ne posent pas cette limitation générale à un seul représentant.
correspondences.note_en: Article 414 limits a party to representation by one person legally authorized to act. Missouri permits specified persons to sue in a representative capacity without joining the beneficiary, but does not impose the same general one-representative limit.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1049 ouvre l’action à toute personne intéressée et au ministère public. RSMo 507.010 et la Rule 52.01 exigent en principe l’action du véritable intéressé, tout en admettant certaines actions représentatives ou autorisées par la loi, sans prévoir expressément le ministère public.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1049 allows any interested person and the public prosecutor to bring the action. RSMo 507.010 and Rule 52.01 generally require prosecution by the real party in interest, while permitting specified representative or statutory actions, but do not expressly provide for a public prosecutor.

norms.heading: Action on claim under foreign law.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS

norms.text:
1. Whenever a claim exists under the law of another state, action thereon may be brought in this state by

(1) The person or persons entitled to the proceeds of such claim if he or they are authorized to bring such action by the laws of said other state;

(2) The executor, administrator, guardian, guardian ad litem or other person empowered by the laws of said other state to sue in a representative capacity if the person or persons entitled to the proceeds of such claim are not authorized to sue in such cases under the law of said other state.

2. In the cases mentioned in subdivision (2), the proceeds of the action, resulting either from judgment or settlement, shall be paid to the person bringing such suit and such person is authorized to satisfy the judgment and execute release. Such person to whom the proceeds are paid shall have authority to distribute and pay same to the person or persons entitled thereto, according to their respective interests therein, under the laws of said other state.

norms.heading: Permissive joinder of parties — separate trials.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text:
1. All persons may join in one action as plaintiffs if they assert any right to relief jointly, severally, or in the alternative in respect of or arising out of the same transaction, occurrence, or series of transactions or occurrences and if any question of law or fact common to all of them will arise in the action. All persons may be joined in one action as defendants if there is asserted against them jointly, severally, or in the alternative, any right to relief in respect of or arising out of the same transaction, occurrence, or series of transactions or occurrences and if any question of law or fact common to all of them will arise in the action. Notwithstanding any other provision of law to the contrary, claims arising out of separate purchases of the same product or service, or separate incidents involving the same product or services shall not satisfy this section. A plaintiff or defendant need not be interested in obtaining or defending against all the relief demanded. Judgment may be given for one or more of the plaintiffs according to their respective rights to relief, and against one or more defendants according to their respective liabilities.

2. The general assembly hereby expressly adopts the holding of State ex rel. Johnson & Johnson v. Burlison, No. SC96704, as issued on February 13, 2019, as it relates to joinder and venue.

3. The court may make such orders as will prevent a party from being embarrassed, delayed, or put to expense by the inclusion of a party against whom he asserts no claim and who asserts no claim against him, and may order separate trials or make other orders to prevent delay or prejudice.
revisor_notes: (2019) Permissive joinder of separate claims cannot and does not "extend venue to a county when, absent joinder, venue in that county would not otherwise be proper for each claim". State ex rel. Johnson & Johnson v. Burlison, 567 S.W.3d 168 (Mo.).

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 323 affirme que chaque cointéressé exerce et supporte individuellement les droits et obligations liés à sa situation dans l’instance. Les textes du Missouri organisent la jonction et permettent un jugement selon les droits ou responsabilités respectifs, sans formuler ce principe général.
correspondences.note_en: Article 323 provides that each co-interested party independently exercises and bears the rights and obligations pertaining to that party’s position in the action. Missouri provisions govern joinder and permit judgments according to each party’s respective rights or liabilities, but do not state the broader principle expressly.

norms.heading: Misjoinder of parties.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text:
1. Misjoinder of parties is not ground for dismissal of an action. Parties may be dropped, added, or severed by order of the court on motion of any party or of its own initiative at any stage of the action and on such terms as are just. Any claim against a party may be severed and proceeded with separately.

2. A motion to drop or add parties may be made at the same time as other motions provided for in section 509.290, and if so made, the provisions of section 509.340 with reference to the consolidation of motions and waiver of objections shall also apply. If said motion is made at any other time, the hearing and determination thereof shall not delay the trial. Objections on account of misjoinder or nonjoinder of parties may also be raised by answer or reply.

correspondences.note_fr: Les demandes reconventionnelles ou additionnelles sont liées aux prétentions originaires par un lien suffisant, tandis que la compensation peut être admise sans ce lien et disjointe si elle retarde excessivement le jugement. La Rule 55.32 traite des demandes reconventionnelles obligatoires ou permissives, la Rule 55.06 de la jonction des demandes et le RSMo 507.050 de leur disjonction. Aucun texte cité ne prévoit expressément l’exception de compensation ni le critère du retard excessif.
correspondences.note_en: Counterclaims and additional claims are connected to the original claims by a sufficient link, while compensation may proceed without that link and be severed if it excessively delays judgment. norms.heading: Persons having claims against plaintiff or plaintiff's insured may be joined as defendants and required to interplead, when — limitation on liability, when — dismissal not required, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text:
1. Persons having claims against the plaintiff or plaintiff's insured may be joined as defendants and required to interplead when their claims are such that the plaintiff is or may be exposed to multiple liability, including multiple claims against the same insurance coverage. It is not ground for objection to the joinder that the claims of the several claimants or the titles on which their claims depend do not have a common origin or are not identical but are adverse to and independent of one another, or that the plaintiff avers that he is not liable in whole or in part to any or all of the claimants. A defendant exposed to similar liability may obtain such interpleader by way of cross-claim or counterclaim. The provisions of this section supplement and do not in any way limit the joinder of parties permitted in section 507.040.

2. For purposes of this subsections 2 to 5 of this section, the term "plaintiff" means the insurer, or any entity which is subject to sections 537.700 to 537.756 or which provides risk management services to any public or private entity, of an insured person or entity subject to more than one claim arising out of any one incident or occurrence, but only when such claims total an amount in excess of the plaintiff's total limits of coverage available for that one incident or occurrence.

3. For purposes of this subsections 2 to 5 of this section, the term "claim" means all actual or potential claims against a plaintiff or plaintiff's insured arising from the one incident or occurrence referred to in subsection 2 of this section.

4. If, within ninety days after receiving the first offer of settlement or demand for payment by a claimant, a plaintiff files an action for interpleader under this section and the plaintiff timely deposits all of its applicable limits of coverage into court within thirty days of the court's order granting interpleader, the plaintiff shall not be liable to any insured or defendant for any amount in excess of the plaintiff's contractual limits of coverage in the interpleader or any other action, so long as the plaintiff defends all of its insureds in good faith from any claims or lawsuits for damages allegedly caused by the incident or occurrence for which the limits of coverage were paid into court, even after depositing its limits of coverage into court notwithstanding any policy provision releasing the plaintiff of its duty to defend any of the insureds. Any insured's refusal of the plaintiff's good faith defense shall not affect the plaintiff's rights under this section.

5. Nothing in this section shall require a release or dismissal of any claim for damages against any insured person or entity upon interpleader by an insurer of that person or entity.

6. Nothing in this section shall be construed, expressly or by implication, to amend, modify, or abrogate any insured's right to consent or control the defense or settlement of any claim as may be provided in any insurance contract.

norms.heading: Class actions — representatives — secondary actions by stockholders — dismissal or compromise.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text:
1. If persons constituting a class are very numerous or it is impracticable to bring them all before the court, such of them, one or more, as will fairly insure adequate representation of all may, on behalf of all, sue or be sued, when the character of the right sought to be enforced for or against the class is

(1) Joint, or common, or secondary in a sense that the owner of a primary right refuses to enforce that right and a member of the class thereby becomes entitled to enforce it;

(2) Several, and the object of the action is the adjudication of claims which do or may affect specific property involved in the action; or

(3) Several, and there is a common question of law or fact affecting the several rights and a common relief is sought. Nothing in this section shall be construed to affect the rights or liabilities of labor unions to sue or be sued.

2. In an action brought to enforce a secondary right on the part of one or more shareholders in an association, incorporated or unincorporated, because the association refuses to enforce rights which may properly be asserted by it, the petition shall aver that the plaintiff was a shareholder at the time of the transaction of which he complains or that his share thereafter devolved on him by operation of law. The petition shall also set forth with particularity the efforts of the plaintiff to secure from the managing directors or trustees and, if necessary, from the shareholders such action as he desires, and the reasons for his failure to obtain such action or the reasons for not making such effort.

3. A class action shall not be dismissed or compromised without the approval of the court. If the right sought to be enforced is one defined in subdivision (1) of subsection 1 notice of the proposed dismissal or compromise shall be given to all members of the class in such manner as the court directs. If the right is one defined in subdivisions (2) or (3) of subsection 1 notice shall be given only after the court requires it.

norms.heading: Third-party notice — when defendant may bring in third party — notice to plaintiff — third party to file petition, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text:
1. Before filing his answer, a defendant may move ex parte or, after the filing of his answer, on notice to the plaintiff, for leave as a third-party plaintiff to file a petition and serve a summons upon a person not a party to the action who is or may be liable to him or to the plaintiff for all or part of the plaintiff's claim against him. If the motion is granted and the petition is filed and summons served, the person so served, herein called the third-party defendant, shall make his defenses, counterclaims and cross-claims against the plaintiff, or any other party as provided in this (civil) code. The third-party defendant may assert any defenses which the third-party plaintiff has to the plaintiff's claim. The third-party defendant is bound by the adjudication of the third-party plaintiff's liability to the plaintiff, as well as of his own to the plaintiff or to the third-party plaintiff. The plaintiff may amend his pleadings to assert against the third-party defendant any claim which the plaintiff might have asserted against the third-party defendant had he been joined originally as a defendant. A third-party defendant may proceed under this section against any person not a party to the action who is or may be liable to him or to the third-party plaintiff for all or part of the claim made in the action against the third-party defendant.

2. When a counterclaim is asserted against a plaintiff, he may cause a third party to be brought in under circumstances which under this section would entitle a defendant to do so.

norms.heading: Intervention — when as of right and when permissive — procedure.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text:
1. Upon timely application anyone shall be permitted to intervene in an action

(1) When a statute confers an unconditional right to intervene; or

(2) When the representation of the applicant's interest by existing parties is or may be inadequate and the applicant is or may be bound by a judgment in the action; or

(3) When the applicant is so situated as to be adversely affected by a distribution or other disposition of property in the custody of the court or of an officer thereof.

2. Upon timely application anyone may be permitted to intervene in an action

(1) When a statute confers a conditional right to intervene; or

(2) When an applicant's claim or defense and the main action have a question of law or fact in common. In exercising its discretion the court shall consider whether the intervention will unduly delay or prejudice the adjudication of the rights of the original parties.

3. (1) A person desiring to intervene shall serve a motion to intervene upon all parties affected thereby. The motion shall state the grounds therefor, and shall be accompanied by a pleading setting forth the claim or defense for which intervention is sought. The same procedure shall be followed when a statute of this state gives a right to intervene.

(2) When the validity of a statute, regulation or constitutional provision of this state, or an ordinance or regulation of a governmental subdivision thereof affecting the public interest is drawn in question in any action to which the state or governmental subdivision or an officer, agency or employee thereof is not a party, the court may in its discretion notify the chief legal officer of the state or subdivision thereof affected.

(3) In all cases and proceedings wherein the validity of a statute, regulation or constitutional provision of this state affecting the public interest is drawn in question, and the state or an officer, agency or employee thereof is not a party, the state of Missouri may in the discretion of the court be permitted to intervene, upon proper application.

(4) In all cases and proceedings wherein the validity of an ordinance or regulation of any governmental subdivision of this state affecting the public interest is drawn in question, and the governmental subdivision, or an officer, agency or employee thereof is not a party, the governmental subdivision may in the discretion of the court be permitted to intervene, upon proper application.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 126 prévoit la régularisation d’un vice avant que le juge statue, notamment par l’entrée en instance de la personne ayant qualité pour agir. Les textes du Missouri permettent la modification d’un acte, l’intervention ou la modification après une demande de rejet, sans reprendre cette règle générale.
correspondences.note_en: Article 126 permits cure of a defect before the court decides, including by the proper party joining the action. The Missouri texts allow amendment, intervention, or amendment after a dismissal motion, but do not reproduce the CPC’s general cure rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise l’information du juge ou du technicien lors de l’intervention d’un tiers et garantit à l’intervenant la possibilité de présenter des observations sur les opérations déjà réalisées. Les règles 52.12 et 507.090 prévoient l’intervention et sa procédure, mais non cette garantie spécifique dans le cadre d’une mesure d’instruction.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires notice to the judge or expert when a third party intervenes and gives the intervenor an opportunity to comment on completed operations. Rules 52.12 and 507.090 govern intervention and its procedure, but do not provide this specific safeguard for an evidentiary measure.

frcp.evidence: Committee Note – 1974 Paragraph (a) is the same as Rule 24(a) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’intervention doit se rattacher aux prétentions des parties par un lien suffisant. Les textes du Missouri régissent l’intervention volontaire, notamment lorsque la demande ou la défense présente une question de droit ou de fait commune, mais ne reprennent pas exactement ce critère général.
correspondences.note_en: Intervention must be connected to the parties’ claims by a sufficient link. The Missouri provisions govern voluntary intervention, including when the application shares a question of law or fact with the main action, but do not reproduce this general threshold exactly.

frcp.evidence: Committee Note – 1974 Paragraph (a) is the same as Rule 24(a) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: Lorsque l’intervention risque de retarder excessivement le jugement, le juge statue d’abord sur la cause principale. RSMo 507.090 impose de prendre en compte le retard indu, tandis que Rule 66.02 permet des procès séparés pour favoriser la célérité, sans prévoir exactement cette priorité de jugement.
correspondences.note_en: When intervention risks excessively delaying judgment, the court decides the main action first. RSMo 507.090 requires consideration of undue delay, while Rule 66.02 permits separate trials to promote expedition, but neither establishes the same priority rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article distingue l’intervention volontaire principale et accessoire. Les textes du Missouri régissent la même institution, mais selon les catégories de l’intervention de droit et de l’intervention permissive, avec des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The article distinguishes principal and accessory voluntary intervention. Missouri governs the same procedural institution, but uses intervention as of right and permissive intervention, with materially different conditions.

frcp.evidence: Committee Note – 1974 Paragraph (a) is the same as Rule 24(a) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’intervention principale élève une prétention propre et exige le droit d’agir à son sujet. Les règles du Missouri prévoient une demande ou défense d’intervention et des critères d’intérêt ou de question commune, sans reprendre expressément cette exigence générale du droit d’agir.
correspondences.note_en: Principal intervention asserts the intervenor’s own claim and requires a right to sue on it. Missouri requires a claim or defense and applies interest or common-question criteria, but does not expressly reproduce that general standing requirement.

frcp.evidence: Committee Note – 1974 Paragraph (a) is the same as Rule 24(a) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: Les textes du Missouri régissent l’intervention fondée sur l’intérêt du demandeur ou sur une question de droit ou de fait commune, mais ne reprennent pas le critère français du soutien accessoire ni le désistement unilatéral.
correspondences.note_en: The Missouri texts govern intervention based on the applicant’s interest or a common question of law or fact, but do not state the French accessory-support criterion or unilateral withdrawal.

frcp.evidence: Committee Note – 1974 Paragraph (a) is the same as Rule 24(a) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut d’office communiquer une affaire au ministère public. La section RSMo 507.090(3)(2) autorise seulement le tribunal à notifier le chief legal officer de l’État ou d’une subdivision lorsque la validité d’une norme d’intérêt public est contestée; son champ est donc beaucoup plus étroit.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may sua sponte refer a matter to the public prosecutor. RSMo 507.090(3)(2) only permits notice to the state or subdivision’s chief legal officer when the validity of a public-interest enactment is challenged, so its scope is much narrower.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 554 permet l’intervention en appel des personnes ayant intérêt, notamment celles qui n’étaient pas parties en première instance ou y figuraient autrement. Les Rule 52.12 et RSMo 507.090 organisent l’intervention fondée sur un intérêt, mais leurs textes ne prévoient pas expressément l’intervention devant la cour d’appel ni l’hypothèse du changement de qualité.
correspondences.note_en: Article 554 permits interested persons to intervene on appeal, including persons who were not parties or were involved in another capacity at first instance. Rule 52.12 and RSMo 507.090 provide interest-based intervention, but do not expressly address appellate intervention or the change-of-capacity situation.

frcp.evidence: Committee Note – 1974 Paragraph (a) is the same as Rule 24(a) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 635 soumet l’intervention des tiers, après cassation, aux règles applicables devant la juridiction dont la décision a été cassée. Rule 52.12 et RSMo 507.090 régissent l’intervention de droit ou facultative et sa procédure, sans prévoir expressément l’effet d’une cassation.
correspondences.note_en: Article 635 subjects third-party intervention after cassation to the rules applicable before the court whose decision was reversed. Rule 52.12 and RSMo 507.090 govern intervention of right, permissive intervention, and procedure, but do not expressly address the post-cassation setting.

frcp.evidence: Committee Note – 1974 Paragraph (a) is the same as Rule 24(a) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 636 permet d’appeler à la nouvelle instance ou d’y intervenir volontairement les personnes parties à l’instance antérieure mais absentes devant la Cour de cassation lorsque leurs droits sont affectés. Les règles du Missouri permettent l’ajout de parties et l’intervention fondée sur un intérêt, mais sans cette condition propre à la cassation.
correspondences.note_en: Article 636 permits former parties who were absent from the court of cassation to be joined in or voluntarily intervene in the new proceeding when their rights are affected. Missouri rules allow parties to be added and interested persons to intervene, but contain no cassation-specific provision.

norms.heading: Substitution of parties upon death, mental incapacity or transfer of interest.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text:
1. (1) If a party dies and the claim is not thereby extinguished, the court shall on motion order substitution of the proper parties. The motion for substitution may be made by the successors or representatives of the deceased party or by any party and, together with the notice of the hearing, shall be served on the parties as provided in section 506.100, and upon persons not parties in the manner provided for the service of a summons.

(2) In the event of the death of one or more of the plaintiffs or of one or more of the defendants in an action in which the right sought to be enforced survives only to the surviving plaintiffs or only against the surviving defendants, the action does not abate. The death shall be suggested upon the record and the action shall proceed in favor of or against the surviving parties.

(3) If the death occurs prior to final judgment or after final judgment and before appeal and substitution or motion therefor is not made within nine months after the first published notice of letters testamentary or of administration, the action shall be dismissed as to the deceased party; if death occurs after appeal and before final determination thereof and substitution or motion therefor is not made in the appellate court where the appeal is pending within nine months after the first published notice of letters testamentary or of administration, the appeal shall be dismissed as to the deceased party.

2. If a party becomes mentally incapacitated, the court upon motion served as provided in subsection 1 may allow the action to be continued by or against his representative.

3. In case of any transfer of interest, the action may be continued by or against the original party, unless the court upon motion directs the person to whom the interest is transferred to be substituted in the action or joined with the original party. Service of the motion shall be made as provided in subsection 1.

4. When a corporation has been sued and served with process or has appeared while in being, and is thereafter dissolved or its charter forfeited, the action shall not be affected thereby and any judgment obtained shall have the effect of a judgment against the last board of directors, in a representative capacity, although the members of the board were not joined in the action.

5. When any public officer is a party to an action and during its pendency dies, resigns, or otherwise ceases to hold office, the action may be continued and maintained by or against his successor upon motion made within one year. Before a substitution is made, the party or officer to be affected, unless expressly assenting thereto, shall be given reasonable notice of the application therefor and accorded an opportunity to object. If no successor is otherwise appointed or elected, the court in which the action is pending may appoint a successor for the prosecution or defense of the action.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 370 prévoit l’interruption, après notification, en cas de décès transmissible, de cessation du représentant légal ou de modification de la capacité d’ester. Les règles 52.13 et RSMo 507.100 organisent plutôt la substitution ou la continuation de l’instance, avec motion et délais; Rule 52.02 encadre la représentation des mineurs.
correspondences.note_en: Article 370 interrupts the action, after notice, for a transmissible death, loss of a legal representative, or a change in capacity to litigate. Rule 52.13 and RSMo 507.100 instead provide for substitution or continuation by motion and subject to deadlines; Rule 52.02 governs minor representation.

correspondences.note_fr: L’instance peut être reprise volontairement selon les formes des moyens de défense ou, à défaut, par citation. Rule 52.13 et RSMo 507.100 prévoient une reprise par motion et notification, avec service comme une assignation dans certains cas, mais sans mécanisme identique de reprise volontaire ou subsidiaire.
correspondences.note_en: The action may be voluntarily resumed through the forms for presenting defenses or, failing that, by citation. Rule 52.13 and RSMo 507.100 provide continuation by motion and notice, with summons-like service in some cases, but not the same voluntary/default resumption mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: Après la reprise, l’instance continue dans l’état où elle se trouvait lors de l’interruption. Rule 52.13 et RSMo 507.100 permettent la continuation de l’action après décès, incapacité ou transfert, mais ne formulent pas expressément cette règle générale de reprise au même état procédural.
correspondences.note_en: After resumption, the action continues in the procedural state existing at interruption. Rule 52.13 and RSMo 507.100 permit continuation after death, incapacity, or transfer, but do not expressly state this general same-state resumption rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 531 interrompt le délai de recours lors d’un changement de capacité ou de certaines procédures collectives, puis le fait courir à compter d’une notification au nouveau destinataire. La Rule 52.13(g), avec les règles de substitution de la Rule 52.13 et du RSMo 507.100, retarde certains délais après jugement jusqu’à la substitution, mais ne reprend pas toutes ces hypothèses.
correspondences.note_en: Article 531 interrupts the appeal period after a change in capacity or certain insolvency proceedings and restarts it upon notice to the person entitled to receive notice. Rule 52.13(g), together with the substitution provisions in Rule 52.13 and RSMo 507.100, delays certain post-judgment periods until substitution, but does not cover all those events.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 532 interrompt le délai de recours au décès, puis prévoit une nouvelle notification au domicile du défunt ou aux héritiers, avec un point de départ lié aux délais successoraux. La Rule 52.13(a) et le RSMo 507.100 organisent la substitution après décès et ses délais, mais selon des mécanismes et délais différents.
correspondences.note_en: Article 532 interrupts the appeal period upon death and provides for renewed notice at the decedent’s domicile or to the heirs, with timing linked to estate-inventory periods. Rule 52.13(a) and RSMo 507.100 govern substitution after death and related deadlines, but use materially different mechanisms and periods.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet de notifier le recours au domicile du défunt et collectivement à ses héritiers, mais exige que chacun soit cité avant qu’un jugement puisse être requis contre eux. Le Missouri prévoit la notification malgré le décès, la substitution et, dans certains cas, la poursuite ou la reprise du jugement contre les héritiers, sans reprendre exactement cette procédure.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits notice of an appeal at the deceased party’s domicile and collectively to heirs, but requires each heir to be summoned before judgment may be sought against them. Missouri addresses notice despite death, substitution, and in some cases continuation or revival against heirs, but not through the same procedure.

norms.heading: Infant defined for civil suit purposes.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text: As used in sections 507.110 to 507.220, the term "infant" means any person who has not attained the age of eighteen years. correspondences.note_en: Article 369 provides several grounds for automatic interruption, including attaining majority and certain insolvency judgments. The Missouri texts address capacity and representation of minors and a receiver-related stay, but do not reproduce the automatic interruption rule or interruption caused by loss of counsel.

norms.heading: Bond of person acting for infant, when — effect of failure to give.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text:
1. Before a next friend or guardian ad litem can receive or receipt for any money or property, personal or real, and before he can acknowledge satisfaction or discharge of any judgment, he must execute a bond to such infant; except, that no bond shall be required if the total value of the property or money, exclusive of expenses and fees approved by the court, is not in excess of ten thousand dollars and all of the money or property is to be turned over to the infant or his parent. The bond must be approved by the court or the clerk thereof and shall be conditioned that the next friend or guardian ad litem shall account to the infant for all money or property which has or does come into his hands, less only those expenses and attorney fees the payment of which has been approved by order of the court. The bond shall be in an amount equal to the value of the money or property if the surety is a corporate bonding, surety or insurance company, and in an amount double the value of the money or property if the surety is not a corporate bonding, surety or insurance company, in which event there shall be two sureties. In either event, the surety or sureties shall be approved by the court or clerk thereof before the bond can be approved.

2. Failure to execute such approved bond with approved surety or sureties when required under the provisions of subsection 1 of this section shall, upon receipt by a next friend or guardian ad litem of any money or property for or on behalf of such minor, immediately render such next friend or guardian ad litem personally liable to the minor for a penal sum in an amount double the value of the money or property and also shall render absolutely void and of no effect any release, receipt or acknowledgment of satisfaction or discharge of any judgment which has or is in the future made or executed by the next friend or guardian ad litem.

3. The next friend's duties or guardian ad litem's duties and his obligations under the bond shall continue until he is discharged therefrom by order of the court.

norms.heading: Powers of next friend, GAL, conservator or guardian on trial and settlement — court approval — settlement of claims permitted.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text:
1. The next friend, guardian ad litem or guardian or conservator shall have the power and authority, subject to the approval of the court, to waive a jury and submit all issues in such action or proposed settlement to the court for determination.

2. The next friend, guardian ad litem or guardian or conservator shall have the power and authority to contract on behalf of the minor for a settlement of the minor's claim, action or judgment, provided that such contract and settlement shall not be effective until approved by the court. The next friend, guardian ad litem and guardian or conservator shall also have the power and authority to execute and sign a release or satisfaction and discharge of a judgment which shall be binding upon the minor, provided the court orders the execution of such release or satisfaction and discharge of judgment.

3. The court shall have the power and authority to hear evidence on and either approve or disapprove a proposed contract to settle an action or claim of a minor, to authorize and order the next friend, guardian ad litem or guardian or conservator to execute and sign a release or satisfaction and discharge of judgment, and shall also have the power and authority to approve a fee contract between the next friend, guardian ad litem or guardian or conservator and an attorney and to order him to pay an attorney fee and to pay the expenses which have been reasonably incurred in connection with the preparation and prosecution of the action or claim and including the cost of any bonds required herein.

4. Notwithstanding the provisions of this section to the contrary, nothing in this section shall be construed as prohibiting the settlement of claims pursuant to section 436.700 or as requiring court approval of settlements pursuant to section 436.700.
revisor_notes: (1973) Judicial settlement of claim against tort-feasors does not release contractual liability of insuror to pay medical expenses to minor not a party to insurance contract. Aetna Casualty and Surety Co. v. Bailey (A.), 497 S.W.2d 816.
(1979) Statute is to be construed to mean persons who have not attained age of 18 years. Holoman v. Harris (A.), 585 S.W.2d 530.

(1981) Judgment entered under provisions of statute for the purpose of effecting a settlement of a minor's cause of action does not bar subsequent suit against persons who were not parties to the action. Arthur v. Evangelical Deaconess Society, etc. (A.), 615 S.W.2d 438.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge chargé d’une mesure d’instruction peut homologuer l’accord mettant fin au litige. La Rule 52.08(e) et le RSMo 507.184 prévoient une approbation judiciaire de certains règlements, mais dans des contextes limités; la Rule 84.02 permet seulement d’explorer un règlement en appel.
correspondences.note_en: The judge overseeing an evidentiary measure may approve an agreement ending the dispute. Rule 52.08(e) and RSMo 507.184 require court approval for certain settlements, but only in limited contexts; Rule 84.02 merely permits settlement exploration on appeal.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 281 prévoit qu’en cas de conciliation pendant l’expertise, l’expert constate que sa mission est devenue sans objet et en informe le juge; les parties peuvent demander que leur accord reçoive force exécutoire. La Rule 88.08 organise un accord écrit issu d’une médiation et son exécution, tandis que les deux sections RSMo prévoient, dans des contextes particuliers, l’approbation ou l’exécution judiciaire d’un règlement.
correspondences.note_en: Article 281 provides that, when the parties settle during the expert process, the expert reports that the mission has become moot; the parties may ask the judge to make their agreement enforceable. Rule 88.08 governs a written mediation settlement and its enforcement, while the two RSMo sections provide court approval or judgment enforcement of settlements in specialized contexts.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 384 prévoit l’extinction accessoire de l’instance par transaction, acquiescement, désistement d’action ou décès dans les actions non transmissibles, constatée par une décision de dessaisissement. Les règles du Missouri traitent surtout du désistement volontaire, de ses effets, du décès d’une partie et, spécifiquement, de l’homologation des transactions concernant les mineurs; elles ne reprennent pas l’ensemble du mécanisme français.
correspondences.note_en: Article 384 provides for incidental termination of the proceeding through settlement, acquiescence, withdrawal of the claim, or death in non-transmissible actions, recorded by a decision divesting the court. Missouri provisions address voluntary dismissal and its effects, death of a party, and—specifically—court approval of minors’ settlements, but do not reproduce the full French mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: Le mandat de représentation est réputé conférer au représentant un pouvoir spécial pour accomplir certains actes procéduraux, notamment le désistement, l’acquiescement, les offres, l’aveu et le consentement. La Rule 55.035 reconnaît une représentation générale, tandis que RSMo 507.184 confère seulement certaines prérogatives de règlement aux représentants de mineurs ou incapables, sous contrôle judiciaire.
correspondences.note_en: The article deems a litigation representative to have special authority for withdrawal, acquiescence, offers, admissions, and consent. Rule 55.035 recognizes general representation, while RSMo 507.184 grants only limited settlement-related powers to representatives of minors or incapacitated persons, subject to court approval.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge homologue l’accord que les parties lui soumettent selon les conditions prévues par le texte référencé. Les textes du Missouri prévoient une approbation judiciaire expresse de certains règlements, notamment en matière de confiscation et de demandes de mineurs.
correspondences.note_en: The French judge approves the agreement submitted by the parties under the conditions of the referenced provision. The Missouri texts require express court approval of certain settlements, notably forfeiture matters and minors’ claims.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge homologue l’accord soumis par les parties. La Rule 88.08 rend un accord écrit de médiation obligatoire sans homologation judiciaire, tandis que RSMo 507.184 prévoit l’approbation judiciaire de certains règlements, notamment ceux concernant les mineurs.
correspondences.note_en: The judge approves an agreement submitted by the parties. Rule 88.08 makes a written mediation settlement binding without judicial approval, while RSMo 507.184 requires court approval for certain settlements, particularly claims involving minors.

correspondences.note_fr: L’homologation est demandée par requête par les parties ou la plus diligente devant le juge compétent, avec décision en principe sans débat. RSMo 513.617 et 507.184 exigent l’approbation judiciaire de certains règlements, mais dans des matières particulières; RSMo 511.740 prévoit une soumission consensuelle au tribunal, avec audition obligatoire.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits the parties, or the more diligent party, to request approval before the seized or otherwise competent judge, normally without a hearing. RSMo 513.617 and 507.184 require court approval of specified settlements, while RSMo 511.740 allows consensual submission to a competent court but requires a hearing.

norms.heading: Substitution of conservator for next friend or guardian ad litem — effect of contracts.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text:
1. At any time during the preparation or prosecution of such action or claim, before or after judgment or appeal, the minor's duly appointed conservator may be substituted for the next friend or guardian ad litem. The substitution may be made by the court or the clerk thereof upon an ex parte showing of the appointment and qualification of the conservator. In the event of such substitution, the court shall, upon payment or transfer of all of the minor's money or property in his hands to the conservator and filing a receipt for the same with a certified copy of the conservator's letters attached to it, and acceptance of the receipt by the court or clerk thereof as authentic, discharge the next friend or guardian ad litem from all of his obligations and duties as such.

2. In the event the minor's conservator has been substituted for the next friend or guardian ad litem and the attorney fees and expenses have not, at the time of the substitution, been paid, the conservator shall be bound by the attorney fee contract and shall be obligated to pay the attorney fees and expenses to the same extent as the next friend or guardian ad litem would have been obligated to pay them had he not been discharged, provided the attorney fees and expenses are approved by the court.

correspondences.note_fr: Le § 507.186 RSMo prévoit, dans le remplacement d’un représentant d’un mineur, le transfert des biens ou fonds au conservateur et la décharge de l’ancien représentant. Il ne traite ni l’action de groupe ni le mandat ou la substitution d’un demandeur défaillant.
correspondences.note_en: RSMo 507.186 provides, when replacing a minor’s representative, for transferring money or property to the conservator and discharging the former representative. It does not address group actions, mandates, or substitution of a defaulting claimant.
